subject: Emotions
title: Memory and Surprise
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Memory and Surprise.

hook.text: You remember where you were on 9/11 but not last Tuesday. Surprise stamps memories with permanent ink.

buildup.text: The amygdala tags surprising events as important. This triggers extra encoding in the hippocampus.

discovery.text: Flashbulb memories feel vivid but aren't always accurate. The emotion is real; the details drift over time.

twist.text: Teachers who open with a surprising fact get better retention than those who start with objectives.

climax.text: Surprise creates a memory advantage called the 'von Restorff effect'—the odd item in a list sticks.

punchline.text: The brain remembers what surprised it. Everything else fades.

quiz.question: What is the von Restorff effect?
options: Odd items in a list are remembered better
